comments.mergedPostDetails: So, what I personally and a few others have requested before me, maybe not on here, is a feature that allows you to see mutual friends. A mutual friends viewer would allow you to know that your friends had met an individual already, and will help improve some people's "clicks."

comments.value: I was gonna post this! Yesss, we need it

I have had to remove people in my friend group from my friends list before to be willing to go green/blue, sometimes temporarily, and the fact that this is not public info meant I only had to explain myself to them - people can be nosy. (I have stayed friends with them on Discord, the meaning of "friend" there is very different.) Also, without privacy controls, this makes it obvious if someone avoids adding one person in particular, both to that person and to the friend group.

In general, I think this could be a nice feature, but it could also create pressures to add (and then not remove) people who you don't actually want joining you, which could in turn push people further away from joinable statuses. I think privacy controls are required at a minimum (Discord has none), as well as thought about whether these dynamics can be mitigated. (For example, this would be less of an issue if you could set your status colour per group of friends.)

One last thing: if this is available on the website, and people start tracking it (as we know people do) and making feeds of who friended or unfriended who, that removes the need for people to even notice changes themselves.

My concern is that the feature request, as currently written, does not consider the right to privacy of the mutual friend at all. If implemented as a mandatory feature, it risks importing the same bullying behaviours we already see on social media and Discord. (The 'guilt by association' drama and 'friend of my enemy' ultimatum bs)

I mean, does anyone really want their best friend to be able to see that they're still 'friends' with said friend's ex?

VRChat doesn’t need to inherit these problems. If this feature must be implemented, it should only ever be opt-in visibility with a bias toward strong privacy controls, rather than arbitrarily forced on all users.
VRChat appear to have now implemented this option in the Privacy section of: https://vrchat.com/home/profile
Please finish rolling out this feature to all users, it would be extremely helpful as a group admin to be able to know who brought somebody new to an event (especially if they're misbehaving)
